name: mailroom
description: Email as a small computer: four VM tools over your real mailboxes, with a credential-holding broker at the tool-call edges.
long_description: A local MCP server that presents email as an environment instead of an API: one RFC 2822 .eml file per message in a Maildir tree, a `mail` CLI for reading, searching, drafting, and queueing sends, and a broker that holds all credentials, enforces send policy (allowlist, rate limit, dry-run), and audits every change. The whole mailbox (100k+ messages) is indexed as metadata in a local SQLite store with full-text search; message bodies download on demand and older ones are evicted under a size quota. Sends never happen directly — the agent queues an intent, the broker validates and delivers when the tool call ends. Mailboxes are connected in-chat with `mail login <address>`: sign-ins happen in your own browser (Microsoft OAuth, or a guided Gmail app-password page); credentials never pass through the chat.

microsoft_client_id.title: Microsoft app (client) ID
microsoft_client_id.description: Azure app registration ID (public client with an http://localhost redirect URI; Graph delegated permissions Mail.ReadWrite + Mail.Send). Only needed for Outlook/Microsoft 365 mailboxes; shared by every Microsoft account. Mailboxes themselves are connected in-chat via `mail login`.

dry_run.title: Dry run (simulate sends)
dry_run.description: When on, everything works except the actual network send — outgoing mail is simulated and ledgered. Turn off only after a test run looks right.

allowed_recipient_domains.title: Allowed recipient domains
allowed_recipient_domains.description: Comma-separated domains mail may be sent to (e.g. example.com, partner.org). Empty = only your own account addresses.

mailroom_home.title: State directory
mailroom_home.description: Where the mail room and broker state live.
